title: Exchange for the normalized projective-line Chern adjunct
statement: Let N>0, let A be a finite commutative ring killed by N, and fix a normalized ordinary finite twist transport t [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Let f:Sprime->S be any morphism of N-invertible schemes. Given c:A_P->A_P(1)[2] and cprime:A_Pprime->A_Pprime(1)[2] satisfying the actual scalar Kummer Chern specifications of O(1) [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class], pullback of the q-adjunct of c, followed by exchange and the shifted line comparison on P, equals the constant comparison on S followed by the qprime-adjunct of cprime. This only concerns the Chern component and asserts no unit-component equation, family existence, decomposition, or invertibility.

source.place: Proof, sentence: Both defining components commute with base change, so the isomorphism does too; expanded by lem-sp-finite-p1-kummer-naturality, steps 1--3

proof.text: On the two projective-line charts the hyperplane x_0=0 has ideal generated by the coordinate x_0/x_1 and by 1, respectively. Multiplication by a polynomial variable is injective over any ring, and remains so after base change. The dual ideal transition is exactly that of the specified O(1). Thus the divisor and its pullback are Cartier with the required associated lines.

proof.text: Use ordinary_supported_kummer for this divisor and its Cartier pullback. Compose its supported morphism with the constant unit. The unit/Chern equation realizes the scalar Kummer boundary of the associated line O(1). The arbitrary-base injectivity of ordinaryFiniteClass identifies these two resulting unsupported morphisms with the given c and cprime. Uniqueness of normalized finite twist transport identifies the supported theorem's transport with t.

proof.text: Compose the supported pullback square with the constant unit and use the divisor mate-unit identity. This gives the unsupported Chern pullback equation with the canonical constant and shifted-line comparisons. Transpose the proposed adjunct equality under qprime inverse image/direct image. The exchange mate-counit identity, naturality and the adjunction triangles turn its two sides into that Chern pullback equation; compatibility of the constant comparisons around the inverse-image square identifies the source. Injectivity of the adjunction correspondence proves the displayed equality.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryFiniteP1_chern_adjunct_baseChange
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {S' S : Scheme.{u}} (f : S' ⟶ S) (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤)))
    (hS' : IsUnit (N : Γ(S', ⊤)))
    (c : ordinaryFiniteUnit A (ProjectiveLine S) ⟶
      (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA (ProjectiveLine S))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (c' : ordinaryFiniteUnit A (ProjectiveLine S') ⟶
      (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA (ProjectiveLine S'))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hc : ordinaryFiniteP1ChernSpec A N hA S
      ((map_natCast (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S).appTop.hom N) ▸
        hS.map (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S).appTop.hom) c)
    (hc' : ordinaryFiniteP1ChernSpec A N hA S'
      ((map_natCast (ProjectiveLine S' ↘ S').appTop.hom N) ▸
        hS'.map (ProjectiveLine S' ↘ S').appTop.hom) c') :
    (ordinaryFinitePullback A f).map (ordinaryFiniteP1ChernPushforward A N hA S c) ≫
        ordinaryFiniteP1Exchange A f
          ((ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA (ProjectiveLine S))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
        (ordinaryFinitePushforward A (ProjectiveLine S' ↘ S')).map
          (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t
            (ProjectiveSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) f)
            ((map_natCast (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S).appTop.hom N) ▸
              hS.map (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S).appTop.hom)).hom =
      (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A f).hom ≫
        ordinaryFiniteP1ChernPushforward A N hA S' c'
